title: A message from Grandma
model: Cambridge A1 Movers / A2 Key – Listening Part 1 (short messages)

script.t: Hello, Sophie. It's Grandma. I'm calling about Saturday. Grandpa and I want to come to your house for lunch. Is that OK? We can arrive at twelve o'clock. I'm going to make a big chocolate cake, because it's your brother's birthday on Sunday. He is eight this year! Grandpa wants to bring his old guitar, so we can sing songs after lunch. Oh, and I've got a present for you too. It's a book about horses. I know you love horses. We are coming by bus, so we don't need a parking place. Please call me back tonight after six. My number is the same: oh one two three, four five six, seven eight nine. See you on Saturday, darling. Lots of love!

questions.prompt: When do the grandparents want to come?
What time will they arrive? (1–3 words)
What is Grandma going to make?
How old will Sophie's brother be? (1–3 words)
What is the present for Sophie?
How are the grandparents travelling?

title: At the fruit shop
model: Cambridge A1 Movers / A2 Key – Listening Part 1 (short dialogues)

script.t: Good morning! Can I help you?
Yes, please. I'd like some apples. The green ones.
How many would you like?
Six, please. And have you got any bananas?
Sorry, no bananas today. They come tomorrow. But we have very nice oranges.
OK, four oranges, please. My children drink orange juice every morning.
Anything else?
Yes, a small bag of tomatoes. How much is that?
The apples are two euros, the oranges are two euros, and the tomatoes are one euro fifty. So that's five euros fifty, please.
Here's ten euros.
Thank you. Here's your change, four euros fifty. Do you want a bag?
No, thank you. I've got my own bag. Goodbye!

questions.prompt: What colour apples does the woman want?
How many apples does she buy? (1–3 words)
Why can't she buy bananas?
What do her children drink every morning?
How much does she pay in total? (1–3 words)
Why doesn't she take a bag from the shop?

title: School announcement
model: Cambridge A1 Movers / A2 Key – Listening Part 2 (announcements)

script.t: Good morning, everyone. This is Mr Brown, the sports teacher. I have some information about Sports Day. Sports Day is next Wednesday, not Thursday. It starts at nine thirty in the morning and finishes at three in the afternoon. Please come to school in your sports clothes and bring a white T-shirt. Every class has a colour, and you can paint your T-shirt in that colour on Monday. There are lots of races: running, jumping and a fun race with eggs and spoons! Parents can come and watch. Please bring a bottle of water and a hat, because it's going to be hot and sunny. Lunch is in the school garden, and the school is giving free ice cream to everyone at the end of the day. Thank you!

questions.prompt: Who is speaking?
Which day is Sports Day? (1–3 words)
What colour T-shirt must students bring?
What is the fun race with?
What must students bring because of the sun? (1–3 words)
What does the school give everyone at the end?

title: My new flat
model: Cambridge A1 Movers / A2 Key – Listening Part 1 (short dialogues)

script.t: Hi Mark! How is your new flat?
I love it, Anna! It's in Green Street, near the park.
Is it big?
Not very big. There's a living room, a small kitchen, one bathroom and two bedrooms.
Two bedrooms? Who sleeps in the second bedroom?
Nobody! It's my music room. I play the piano there.
Nice! What's your favourite room?
The kitchen. It's small, but it has a big window and I can see the park. I have breakfast there every morning.
Is the flat on the ground floor?
No, it's on the fifth floor, and there's no lift! But it's good exercise.
Can I come and see it?
Of course. Come on Sunday afternoon. I can make pizza.

How many bedrooms does the flat have?

title: Weekend weather
model: Cambridge A1 Movers / A2 Key – Listening Part 2 (radio)

script.t: And now, the weather for the weekend. On Friday evening, it's cloudy and a little cold, about ten degrees. On Saturday morning, it's going to rain in the north, so take your umbrella if you go out. In the south, it's dry but windy. In the afternoon, the rain stops and the sun comes out everywhere. On Sunday, it's a beautiful day. It's sunny and warm all day, about twenty-two degrees. It's a perfect day to go to the beach or have a picnic in the park. But be careful on Sunday night, because there may be a storm in the west. On Monday, the weather is cold and cloudy again, so remember your coat when you go to work or school. That's all for today. Have a great weekend!

What should you take on Saturday morning in the north? (1–3 words)
What is the weather like in the south on Saturday morning?
What will the temperature be on Sunday? (1–3 words)

title: Making plans
model: Cambridge A1 Movers / A2 Key – Listening Part 1 (short dialogues)

script.t: Tom, are you free on Friday evening?
Yes, I am. Why?
There's a new film at the cinema. It's a comedy about a dog. Do you want to come?
Sounds fun! What time is it?
There are two times, six o'clock and eight thirty.
I finish work at six, so eight thirty is better for me.
OK. The tickets are eight euros. I can buy them online.
Great, thanks. Shall we eat something before the film?
Yes! There's a nice Chinese restaurant next to the cinema.
Perfect. Let's meet at the restaurant at seven. Oh, and can I bring my sister? She loves dogs, and she loves comedies too.
Of course! I can buy three tickets. She can come to the restaurant too. OK. See you on Friday!

What animal is the film about? (1–3 words)

How much are the tickets? (1–3 words)

title: At the train station
model: Cambridge A1 Movers / A2 Key – Listening Part 2 (announcements)

script.t: Good afternoon. This is an announcement for passengers travelling to London. The two fifteen train to London is late. It is now leaving at two forty-five from platform six, not platform three. We are very sorry. The train to Oxford is on time. It leaves at two thirty from platform one. Passengers for Oxford, please go to platform one now. There is no food on the train to London today, but you can buy sandwiches and drinks at the café next to platform four. The café is open until ten o'clock tonight. Please keep your bags with you at all times. If you need help, please ask a member of staff in a yellow jacket. Toilets are next to the ticket office. Thank you, and have a good journey.

title: My day
model: Cambridge A1 Movers / A2 Key – Listening Part 3 (talk)

script.t: Hi, I'm David and I'm a baker. My day starts very early. I get up at four o'clock in the morning, when everyone is asleep! I have a cup of coffee, but I don't eat breakfast at home. I walk to the bakery. It's only five minutes from my house. I start work at half past four. I make bread, cakes and cookies. My favourite thing to make is apple cake. The shop opens at seven, and lots of people buy bread for breakfast. I finish work at one o'clock. Then I go home and have lunch with my wife. In the afternoon, I sleep for two hours. In the evening, I play football with my friends on Tuesdays and Thursdays. I go to bed at nine o'clock every night.

title: At the doctor's
model: Cambridge A1 Movers / A2 Key – Listening Part 1 (short dialogues)

script.t: Good morning. What's the problem?
I feel terrible, doctor. I've got a headache and a sore throat.
When did it start?
Two days ago, on Monday.
Have you got a temperature?
Yes, a little. Thirty-eight degrees this morning.
OK. I think you have a cold. It's not serious. Drink a lot of water and hot tea with honey. Take these tablets two times a day, after breakfast and after dinner.
Can I go to work?
No, stay at home and rest for three days. If you don't feel better on Friday, come back and see me.
Can I eat normal food?
Yes, but eat light food, like soup and fruit. And don't go out in the cold. Sleep a lot. That is the best medicine.
Thank you, doctor.

questions.prompt: What problems does the man have?
options: A headache and a sore throat

How many days must he stay at home? (1–3 words)

title: Holiday message
model: Cambridge A1 Movers / A2 Key – Listening Part 1 (short messages)

script.t: Hi Jack, it's Emma. I'm on holiday in Spain with my family. We're in a small town near the sea. The weather is fantastic, it's hot and sunny every day. Our hotel is very nice. It has a big swimming pool, and my room has a balcony with a view of the beach. Every morning, I swim in the sea with my sister. The water is warm and very clean. In the afternoon, we sleep, because it's too hot to go out. In the evening, we eat in a restaurant in the town square. I love the fish here! Tomorrow we're going on a boat trip to see dolphins. I'm very excited. We come home next Saturday. See you soon! Bye!
